definition: The direct line of cell division or evolutionary descent linking a progenitor stem cell to its specialized progeny.
etymology: From Old French lignage, from ligne ('line').
manuscriptExample: Single-cell lineage tracing mapped embryonic neural crest cell migration into peripheral autonomic ganglia.
conferenceExample: The reviewer commended the manuscript for validating lineage commitment markers across multiple differentiation stages.

definition: Light emission from a chemical or enzymatic reaction not resulting from heat, widely used in reporter gene assays.
manuscriptExample: Bioluminescence signal intensity was monitored in real-time using a CCD camera imaging chamber.
conferenceExample: The section editor asked for vehicle luminescence baselines to verify signal specificity.
